fact: 1904年4月8日，英法在伦敦签署一系列协议即“协约国协定”（Entente Cordiale），由三份文件组成：关于埃及与摩洛哥的声明、关于纽芬兰与西中非的协议、关于暹罗（泰国）与新赫布里底的总声明，显著改善了英法关系。

sources.title: Wikipedia — Entente Cordiale
sources.quote: The Entente Cordiale ... comprised a series of agreements signed on 8 April 1904 between the United Kingdom and France which saw a significant improvement in Anglo-French relations. / The Entente was composed of three documents: The first and most important document was the Declaration respecting Egypt and Morocco. In return for the French promising not to "obstruct" British actions in Egypt, the British promised to allow the French to "preserve order ... and provide assistance" in Morocco.

fact: 协约国协定的领土交换：法国放弃《乌得勒支条约》以来对纽芬兰西岸（French Shore）的权利（保留捕鱼权）以换取英国在西非的让步；在暹罗以湄南河为界划分英法势力范围；法国不阻挠英国在埃及行动、英国允许法国在摩洛哥“维持秩序”。

sources.title: Wikipedia — Entente Cordiale
sources.quote: The second document dealt with Newfoundland and portions of West and Central Africa. The French gave up their rights (stemming from the Treaty of Utrecht) over the western coast of Newfoundland, known as the French Shore, although they retained the right to fish the coast. / In Siam, the British recognised a proposed French sphere of influence to the east of the Menam (Chao Phraya) River basin; in turn, the French recognised a proposed British influence over the territory to the west of the Menam basin. / The Entente was composed of three documents: The first and most important document was the Declaration respecting Egypt and Morocco. In return for the French promising not to "obstruct" British actions in Egypt, the British promised to allow the French to "preserve order ... and provide assistance" in Morocco.

fact: 日俄战争中，日本战争总支出的相当部分从英国、加拿大与美国借入：高桥是清在伦敦筹资，Jacob Schiff提供2亿美元贷款并从英国罗斯柴尔德家族融资——1904年的伦敦资本市场是对日战争融资的主渠道。

sources.title: Wikipedia — Russo-Japanese War（Economics节）
sources.quote: Japan's pre-war gold reserves were a modest £11.7 million; a major portion of the total cost of the war was covered by money borrowed from the United Kingdom, Canada, and the United States. During his canvassing expedition in London, the Japanese vice-governor of the Bank of Japan Takahashi Korekiyo met Jacob Schiff, an American banker and head of Kuhn, Loeb & Co. ... extended a critical series of loans to the Empire of Japan, in the amount of 200 million US dollars (£41.2 million). He also raised loans from the Rothschild family in Britain.

fact: 伦敦证券交易所的会员分为面向公众的broker（经纪人）与只与其他会员成交的jobber（做市商），公众须经broker下单，成交按约半月结算交割——1904年进入伦敦股市的合法通道是持有牌照的broker。

sources.title: 1911 Encyclopædia Britannica / Stock Exchange (Wikisource)
sources.quote: The London Stock Exchange is remarkable for having developed spontaneously a special mode of doing business, namely the differentiation of members into jobbers and brokers. A jobber is a member of the Stock Exchange who, according to the rules of that body, does business only with other members, as opposed to a broker who does business with the public as well as with his fellow members. ... The interval between two settlements varies from 12 days to 19 days, but the normal interval is 14 days ... In most securities it would not be easy to deal "for money" ... but this can always be done in consols and other British government securities

fact: 1905年《外国人法》之前英国没有和平时期入境管制：1826—1905年英国边境开放，内政部统计口径下不存在现代意义上的移民配额——1904年入境英国几乎不受限制。

sources.title: Refugees: English Law's Protection or Persecution? (Prof. Leslie Thomas, Gresham College lecture, 2024)
sources.quote: From a practical perspective, therefore, between 1826 and 1905 there were no immigration controls as we know them today. The UK had open borders. In fact, the Foreign Secretary, Lord Granville, said in a directive to all British missions in 1852: "By the existing laws of Great Britain, all foreigners have the unrestricted right of entrance and residence in this country … No foreigner, as such, can be sent out of the country by the Executive Government"

fact: 1870年《入籍法》规定：外国人须在英国居住满五年（或从事王室服务相应年限）并具良好品行方可归化；归化者取得与本土出生者基本相同的政治与财产权利——1904年的身份路线是五年居住加归化申请。

sources.title: Control of Enemy Alien Civilians in Great Britain (LSE Theses Online, U322824)
sources.quote: When the war began British nationality regulations derived from the Naturalisation Act of 1870 ... The act laid down a requirement of five year residence in Britain or crown service as qualifications for naturalisation, but it gave the subject the right to sit in parliament or on the Privy Council

fact: 伦敦码头日工的长期工资基准是1889年罢工争得的日工6便士（docker's tanner）、加班8便士；该标准写入协议后延续至1900年代——无技能外来者在伦敦码头的日收入锚点约6便士。

sources.title: The 1889 London dockers' & tailors' strikes | London Museum
sources.quote: The demand for increased rates of pay to be 6d or 'tanner' ( around £2 now) per hour for day work with 8d per hour overtime resulted in the strike being referred to as the 'dockers' tanner'. ... The agreement conceded most of the dockers' demands, including the 'dockers tanner'.

fact: 查尔斯·布斯伦敦调查所记东区“极贫阶层”每人周均收入5先令1便士，其中房租1先令3便士、食物3先令7便士——1904年伦敦东区的生存底线预算是可参照的贫困线数据。

sources.title: Early Innovations in Social Research: The Poverty Survey of Charles Booth (Bales, LSE Theses Online)
sources.quote: The average income per adult per week among the "very poor" was 5s 1d; rent would take 1s 3d of this and food a further 3s 7d.

fact: 英国登记商船在1900年占世界商船总吨位约45%，伦敦港的码头、船运与相关服务业构成庞大就业部门；航运是英国最大的产业之一，也是外来劳动力的主要吸纳器。

sources.title: The Decline of British Shipping: Some New Perspectives (Davies, PhD thesis, University of Warwick, WRAP)
sources.quote: In terms of British registered shipping as a proportion of the world fleet, a decline can be noted from 1900 which was when British-registered shipping dominated global commerce and provided 45% of world tonnage (Sturmey, 1962).

fact: 《每日邮报》1896年创刊，到1900年前后日发行量已达约100万份，是当时全球销量最大的日报；廉价大众报业与电影放映（1896年创刊号即刊登卢米埃尔 Cinematograph 广告）同步成长，1904年的伦敦是大众传媒与新式娱乐的试验场。

sources.title: Early Edition: the Daily Mail, British newspapers, and the moving image, 1896-1922 (Tom Rice, University of St Andrews)
sources.quote: The first edition of the Daily Mail on May 4 1896 included an advertisement for the "latest scientific marvel,"the Lumiere Cinematograph. ... The concurrent growth of the Daily Mail –which with a daily circulation of one million by 1900 was the largest selling newspaper in the world –is the most striking example of a new popular,affordable press.
